title: Outcome after neurorehabilitative treatment of stroke: Comparative observational study in Germany and Kazakhstan.
summary: This observational study investigates the effectiveness of neurorehabilitation measures after stroke in Germany and Kazakhstan. It focuses on how specific rehabilitation methods affect patients' functional recovery, particularly regarding motor skills, daily independence, and overall quality of life. To answer this, 180 patients from both countries are followed and evaluated over six months using various standardized assessments conducted at the beginning of the neurorehabilitation, two weeks post-neurorehabilitation, and three and six months after the stroke. These assessments include the Barthel Index for evaluating daily competence and specific tests for cognitive and motor skills. The study aims not only to shed light on the effectiveness of the rehabilitation measures applied but also to contribute to improving treatment standards in stroke aftercare internationally.
conditions: Stroke, not specified as haemorrhage or infarction

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- First stroke
- Time since the event: < 4 weeks
- Moderately affected patients based on a Barthel Index >40 and ≤ 70 at study inclusion
- Ability to understand basic instructions and information
- Willingness to participate by the patient or their carer
- Knowledge of the type of stroke (ischaemic / haemorrhagic)
Exclusion criteria:
- Presence of a serious, life-shortening other illness (e.g. cancer, severe heart failure, severe lung disease)
- Presence of a severe psychiatric illness
- Presence of other neurological diseases
- Pain during physical activity (visual analogue scale > 5)
- Gastric tube, percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy
